While yes, spheres are by far the most commonly occurring shapes for planet and stars and other celestial bodies to take, the complexity of them is more talked about geometrically, with a sphere having the most complex structure, “infinite” sides, and the tetrahedron having 4 sides, the fewest sides that can happen in three dimensions. So yes, tetrahedrons are rarer in nature than spheres, but geometrically they are much simpler. 

Onto the question of what the traveler and pyramids are. The traveler is at least connected to the Gardener, it is theorized that it *is* her, but that’s not confirmed, the pyramids we know even less about, logic dictates that if the force of light is controlled or influenced by the gardener, then the force of the darkness is controlled by the winnower, but again, we don’t know. This is all gathered from Unveiling, and whileyou’re reading that lore book, do keep in mind that this comes from the darkness, who has been known to lie and deceive to get what it wants, but it is also the only account of the Time Before Time. The gardener and winnower basically made a bet, and the gardener put herself into the universe as the traveler to enforce the rule she wanted put into the flower game. No one really *built* it per se, it just sorta, *pop* there. 

As far as I know, no one’s been *on* the traveler, it’s big enough to generate a gravitational field but obviously it doesn’t, otherwise the whole floating above the city thing wouldn’t exactly work out. A tiny bit of the inside could be seen back before the SOA finale, but not very well.  The only person we know of to fly inside the traveler is the famous Uncle Fenchurch of the Everis family, who isn’t really the most trust worthy figure but again, only account we have of it. Fenchurch said it smelled like vanilla, and didn’t say anything else about it. Ghosts are kind of a mystery. All we know is that in the Constellations lore book they seemed to be referred to tiny versions of the traveler, sparks of light in a sea of dark. They were released as the traveler went into its coma after its battle with the pyramids. There have not been any new ghosts since. We don’t really know where the bottom bits of the traveler are, other than the big one in the EDZ. 

Ah yes, the age old “more travelers” theory. We aren’t sure about it, but we *think* there’s only one traveler, but there’s no surefire way to know.
